data.title: Strategy buys 2,789 Bitcoin for fourth consecutive week
data.description:
Strategy has now bought Bitcoin four weeks in a row, adding a combined 2,789 BTC to what was already the largest corporate stash of the asset on the planet.

The most recent purchase was a modest one by Strategy standards. Between November 16 and 22, 2026, the company picked up 457 BTC for approximately $29.6 million.

That brings Strategy's total holdings to 851,305 BTC as of November 22. The company has spent around $64.23 billion building that pile, which works out to an average of about $75,446 per coin.

Here is where the math gets uncomfortable. During the latest purchase window, Bitcoin was trading near $63,000.

Put plainly, the average coin in Strategy's vault cost more than the market will currently pay for it. The position is underwater relative to its cost basis, at least on paper.

Strategy remains the largest public holder of Bitcoin, sitting on nearly 4% of the asset's total supply cap. That is a remarkable share for a company that, under its old name MicroStrategy, was known for business intelligence software.

The funding for this round came from Strategy's at-the-market offering, usually shortened to ATM. During the same week, Strategy sold 1.93 million shares of its Class A common stock through that program. Net proceeds came to $176.7 million.

Only a small slice of that went toward Bitcoin. The bigger use of cash was a repurchase of about 2.18 million shares of its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred Stock, ticker STRC, for approximately $211.8 million.

That buyback figure is larger than the week's ATM proceeds. In other words, Strategy spent more retiring preferred stock than it raised from selling common stock, and far more than it spent on Bitcoin.

So the week's story is less "company buys Bitcoin" and more "company tidies up its balance sheet, and also buys some Bitcoin." The 457 BTC was the side dish.

The most immediate takeaway is that Strategy appears to be prioritizing capital structure over raw accumulation right now. Spending more on the STRC buyback than on Bitcoin in a single week is a meaningful shift in emphasis, even if the purchases continue.

The cost basis is the other pressure point. With Bitcoin trading near $63,000 against an average purchase price of about $75,446, Strategy is carrying an unrealized loss on its core asset.

As the largest public Bitcoin treasury company, Strategy's moves are widely read as a signal of institutional conviction. Continued buying through a drawdown suggests the company has not lost faith in its thesis, and the research suggests that persistence could encourage other institutions to consider similar strategies.

What to watch next is fairly simple. Track whether the weekly buying streak continues, how much of each ATM raise actually reaches Bitcoin versus preferred stock buybacks, and whether MSTR regains any premium to its holdings.

data.title: Baltic index inches down as capesize segment weakens
data.description:
The Baltic Exchange's main sea freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, fell on Friday as rates for larger capesize vessels edged lower, but still posted a weekly gain.

  • The main Baltic index , tracking rates of capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, fell 15 points, or 0.48%, to 3,137 points but marked a gain of 4.6% for the week

  • The capesize index (.BACI) fell by 77 points, or 1.51%, to 5,023 points, but was up 5.1% for the week

  • Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-metric-ton cargoes including iron ore and coal, fell $692 to $42,055

  • Iron ore prices erased some earlier losses to trade slightly lower, as Beijing vowed stronger market support, bolstering investor sentiment and offsetting downward pressure

  • The panamax index (.BPNI) inched up 42 points to 2,315 points, recording a weekly gain of 7.7%

  • Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, rose by $378 to $20,834

  • The supramax index (.BSIS), for smaller vessels, was up 2 points, or 0.1%, to 1,818 points and gained 0.5% for the week

data.description:
RNS Number : 0346F Eco Hotels UK PLC 27 November 2026  

Eco Hotels UK Plc

27 November 2026

ECO HOTELS UK PLC APPOINTS VINOD TRIPATHI AS ADVISOR TO THE BOARD

Appointment of Vinod Tripathi as Advisor to the Board

To oversee the execution of the expansion of the Eco brands across other emerging markets

South East Asia and Africa in view after the build out of the India platform

Corporate update

Eco Hotels UK Plc ('Eco Hotels' or the 'Company'), the world's first carbon neutral hotel brand of its kind, today announces the appointment of Vinod Tripathi as Advisor to the Board with immediate effect. Mr Tripathi will oversee the execution of the expansion of the Eco brands across other emerging markets, with South East Asia and Africa as the first regions in view.

Mr Tripathi set up the group's hotel operations in India as Executive Chairman of Eco Hotels and Resorts Limited ('EHRL'), the BSE listed company (BSE: 514402) of which Eco Hotels is the promoter. During his tenure EHRL built an inventory of nine existing hotels and one greenfield hotel. He stepped down as Executive Chairman of EHRL in November 2026.

Key Points

•          Vinod Tripathi appointed Advisor to the Board of Eco Hotels UK Plc

•          He will oversee the execution of the expansion of the Eco brands across other emerging markets

•          South East Asia and Africa are the first regions in view

•          Mr Tripathi set up the operations in India and built an inventory of nine existing hotels and one greenfield hotel

•          The appointment brings that operating experience into the holding company, which holds the Eco brands

•          India will continue to be served through EHRL

Corporate Strategy

Eco Hotels' vision is a premium value hotel chain that offers sustainable hospitality without compromising the guest experience. India was the first market for the brands, through EHRL. The Company now intends to take the brands into other emerging markets where demand for affordable, branded and sustainable hotel rooms is growing.

Mr Tripathi will advise the Board on the choice of markets, the local partners and the plan for execution in each market. The Company expects to enter new markets through leases, management contracts and franchise agreements with local owners, in line with the asset light model used in India. Further announcements will be made as markets and partners are agreed.

Management Quotes

Vinod Tripathi, Advisor to the Board of Eco Hotels UK Plc, said: "When I joined Eco Hotels the task was to set up the operations in India from a standing start. Today there is an inventory of nine existing hotels and one greenfield hotel, and a team that knows how to open and run hotels to the Eco standard. I now look forward to giving my input to the Board as the brand expands into South East Asia and Africa. The need for good, affordable and sustainable hotels in those markets is every bit as real as it is in India."

Arvid Pedersen, Director of Eco Hotels UK Plc, said: "I am pleased to have Vinod's participation in the holding company. He set up our operations in India and built the portfolio hotel by hotel, and that is the experience we want around the table as we take the Eco brands into other emerging markets. With Vinod advising the Board, we can turn our plans for South East Asia and Africa into hotels on the ground."

About Eco Hotels UK Plc

Eco Hotels UK Plc (Co. No. 06584439) is a UK public limited company with its registered office at 16 Berkeley Street, London W1J 8DZ. It holds the Eco hotel brands, which include The Eco, The Eco Satva, Ecoxpress, Ecoxpress Satva and Ecovalue. It is the promoter of Eco Hotels and Resorts Limited, which is listed on BSE (514402) and operates hotels in India under those brands. Eco Hotels is a subsidiary of Red Ribbon Asset Management Plc ('Red Ribbon Group'), the Indo British impact investment group founded in 2007.

About Vinod Tripathi

Vinod Kumar Tripathi is a career bureaucrat and technocrat with more than four decades of experience across government, the public sector and the private sector. He began his career in the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and went on to serve the Government of India as a Commissioner of Income Tax, with his last posting in Mumbai.

He is a turnaround specialist. As Managing Director of National Textiles Corporation (Maharashtra, South and Gujarat) he turned around one of India's large textile companies. He then spent a decade and a half in financial services, where he was President and Group Director at Reliance Capital Limited. He also served as an Independent Director of Easy Trip Planners Limited from 2020 to 2026.

In 2022 he joined EHRL as Executive Chairman. He set up its hotel operations in India and established the initial inventory of nine existing hotels and one greenfield hotel.

data.title: US stocks set for higher open as battered AI shares claw back losses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 1.42%, S&P 1.64%, Nasdaq 2.31%
  • Chipmakers, AI hyperscalers and neoclouds jump
  • Gold and silver miners rally, tracking metals price recovery

By Shashwat Chauhan and Avinash P

Wall Street's main indexes were set for a higher open on Friday, with the Nasdaq poised to outperform as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday break and rushed back into battered AI-linked shares.

US stocks have swung sharply this week, with Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and Anthropic's brief fall below its IPO price adding to volatility across the AI trade.

Investors have alternated between bargain-hunting after a steep selloff and concerns over soaring costs, heavy borrowing and whether the investments are generating sufficient returns.

"(Investors) felt that the selloff that we saw going into last Friday was overdone. It would be more of a steady push up from here, possibly," said David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation.

Despite the turbulence, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are headed for their best week since April and August, respectively, while the blue-chip Dow is on track for its strongest week since April 2025.

However, the gains have done little to erase November's losses. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq are on course for their worst November since 2008, pressured by concerns over tougher AI regulation following the Democrats' midterm election victory and expectations that monetary policy will remain restrictive.

Investors are also assessing the impact of the Trump administration's proposed new tariffs on imports from 14 trading partners, announced on Wednesday.

Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December after data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated further in October.

All three major indexes entered a technical correction this month, with the Nasdaq 100 at one point falling nearly 20% from its October peak.

At 8:25 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were up 711 points, or 1.42%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 118.25 points, or 1.64%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 603 points, or 2.31%.

Nvidia, at the center of the AI boom, gained 2.3% in premarket trading, though the stock remained more than 37% below its October record high based on its last close.

Other chipmakers that were battered this month also rebounded, with AMD climbing 4.4% and Broadcom gaining 3.6%.

AI hyperscalers Alphabet , Amazon.com , Microsoft , Meta Platforms and Oracle rose between 1.9% and 3.8%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius advanced 5.4% and 6.9%, respectively. Other AI beneficiaries, including data-storage firm Sandisk , optical-products maker Lumentum <LITE.O> and server maker Dell , also gained.

Gold and silver miners rallied as precious-metal prices recovered from a bruising few sessions. Newmont gained 4.4%, while the Global X Silver Miners ETF advanced 5.2%.

Altria fell 2.5% after the US Marlboro maker said it was considering an all-cash bid for Imperial Brands and was discussing a deal involving part of the British tobacco group's business with another party.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals slid 8.1% after the US Food and Drug Administration extended its review of the company's kidney-disease drug by up to three months.

Trading volumes could be light following Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday, with US equity markets open for only a half day on Friday.

data.title: German lower house of parliament passes 2027 budget
data.description:
By Maria Martinez

Germany's lower house of parliament passed a €556 billion ($610 billion) 2027 budget on Friday, which includes higher defence spending, heavy investment and the second-highest level of new borrowing in the country's history.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government has vowed a push to strengthen Germany's core infrastructure and rebuild its military after decades of underinvestment.

Total new borrowing will reach €210.4 billion, just under the record €215.4 billion recorded in 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic, budget figures showed.

That includes new borrowing of some €123 billion from the core budget, which does not include additional debt authorised under special measures to allow greater spending on infrastructure and defence agreed last year.

"It is right that we invest in the railways and in climate protection. It is right ... that we invest in our security," Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said on Friday in parliament.

Investment in the core budget is set at €61.8 billion, up from €58.4 billion in 2026. Additional investment will come from special funds.

Core defence spending will rise to €109.7 billion from €82.2 billion in 2026. The total reaches €150.9 billion, including support for Ukraine and other security spending.

"We are putting up the money for defence so that Ukraine can defend its freedom," Klingbeil said. "No child born in Germany today should ever have to experience war again."

data.title: RBI Deputy Governor urges banks to speed up MSME lending, expand cash-flow-based credit
data.description:
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Deputy Governor Swaminathan J on November 27 urged banks to expedite credit sanctions to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and reduce their reliance on collateral by expanding cash-flow-based lending through the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and other digital channels.

Chairing the 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) on the flow of credit to the MSME sector in Kolkata, Swaminathan also called for greater use of the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) to finance MSME receivables, along with early identification and resolution of stress among borrowers.

He urged industry associations to participate in the RBI's town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings to improve awareness and raise their members' concerns with banks.

The committee reviewed working capital and investment credit to MSMEs, lending to first-time borrowers and credit guarantee coverage. Discussions also covered the higher limit for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises, settlement of invoices by central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) through TReDS and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026.

The meeting was attended by representatives of the Ministry of MSME, Ministry of Finance, banks, SIDBI, NABARD, CGTMSE, NCGTC, KVIC and MSME industry associations.

data.title: European luxury braces for another bumpy and uneven year—J.P. Morgan
data.description:
The European luxury space could face another challenging year, says J.P. Morgan analysts Chiara Battistini and Wendy Liu, as consumer spending is still resilient but discriminating.

This will be especially notable in China, where high net worth individuals will continue to spend while "aspirational customers" will shift their share of wallet towards brands with sharp, authentic execution.

The analysts see jewelry and ready-to-wear remaining as bright spots, while luxury goods will experience a “bumpy” year as demand will be driven by brand strength.

Against this backdrop, their stock picking remains selective, calling out Richemont as a top pick in luxury.

Battistini and Liu remain Overweight on Brunello Cucinelli , Zegna Group , and Moncler .

Swatch and Pandora (upgraded to Overweight) are both placed on J.P. Morgan’s Positive Catalyst Watch with Pandora buoyed by declining silver prices and signs of better brand momentum.

Kering retains its Underweight rating as the “most challenging story in leather goods,” given that the Gucci revamp is expected to take longer than hoped and will likely delay a return to growth to the second half of next year.

In sporting goods, Puma was downgraded to Underweight and adidas to Neutral amid sector headwinds.

Lastly, the analysts remain cautious towards both LVMH Moet Hennessy-Louis Vuitton and Hermès with both lacking an imminent catalyst for re-rating.

data.title: ASTS Stock’s New Target By Berenberg Shows A 67% Cut – Analyst Says Satellite Launch Delays Hurt Revenue Ramp
data.description:
Key points:
  • The firm said it expected the company to expand its satellite network to 248 satellites faster.
  • Berenberg identified a successful return to flight of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket as a potential catalyst for revisiting its rating.
  • AST SpaceMobile recently partnered with Firefly Aerospace to develop its own reusable rocket and reduce dependency on third-party launch providers.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) received a downgrade from Berenberg on Friday due to a delay in its revenue ramp, with the brokerage highlighting the challenges in satellite launches.

Berenberg downgraded ASTS to ‘Hold’ from ‘Buy’ and slashed its price target by 67% to $30 from $92, according to an Investing.com report. This represents a 12% upside from current levels.

ASTS shares were up 3% at the time of writing.

Berenberg Expects ASTS To Generate Positive Free Cash Flow In 2030

According to the report, Berenberg said it was “too early” to initiate AST SpaceMobile coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating in September, when it expected the company to expand its satellite network to 248 satellites faster.

The firm had anticipated that revenue from early satellite deployments would help finance further expansion. However, launch delays have pushed back those expectations.

Berenberg now expects AST SpaceMobile to deploy around 100 satellites by 2028 and maintain its network at that level until it generates positive free cash flow in 2030. However, the firm said that it remains confident in the company’s technology and long-term business prospects.

Why Blue Origin’s New Glenn Is Crucial

Berenberg believes much of AST SpaceMobile’s expansion depends on launch capacity provided by Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin. In April, Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket failed to place AST SpaceMobile’s BlueBird 7 satellite into orbit.

Berenberg said a successful return to flight could prompt it to reconsider its rating, while another failure or extended delay could put further pressure on the stock.

Earlier this month, AST SpaceMobile said it was targeting a Blue Origin launch carrying three BlueBird satellites in early 2027.

AST SpaceMobile Looks To Reduce Reliance On Launch Providers

However, AST SpaceMobile is planning to reduce dependency on third-party launch vehicles. Earlier this month, the company announced a partnership with Firefly Aerospace (FLY) to develop its own reusable rocket, Blacklift. Under the agreement, Firefly will provide engine technology and supply engines for Blacklift’s first three launches.

The rocket is designed to carry up to five BlueBird satellites per mission, with launches targeted to begin in late 2028. This also gives AST SpaceMobile greater control over its satellite deployment schedule.

Retail Remains Bearish On ASTS

Retail sentiment surrounding ASTS on Stocktwits remained ‘bearish’ over the past 24 hours.

ASTS shares have declined about 67% so far in 2026.

data.title: Stock Futures Jump as AI Trade Set for Rebound — Update
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

U.S. stock indexes are poised to open in the green for a shortened trading session Friday, as the artificial-intelligence trade rebounds at the end of a volatile week.

Nasdaq futures traded 2% higher, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.4% and 1.2%, respectively. If the gains hold to market close, the indexes will close a choppy week with gains of more than 4% each. Still, they remain well below their recent highs: The S&P 500 and Dow are each over 6% below their early October peaks, while the Nasdaq, down more than 14% over the same period, is still in a correction.

Signs of a rebound follow choppy trade earlier in the week. Stocks across the AI ecosystem rallied premarket, with Nvidia gaining over 3%, while chip makers and data-center providers looked set for strong opens. However, the AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, Amati Global Investors fund manager Mikhail Zverev said.

"We still haven't got answers to the biggest questions we are asking," the fund manager said. Concerns include "higher interest rates and the expanding cost of funding for the AI buildout," Zverev added.

Gains in the U.S. premarket followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's memory-chip-dominated Kospi jumped 4.3%, while stock indexes in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. European equity indexes rallied at the open, with AI-related stocks leading the charge. The continent's Stoxx 600 index rose 0.9% in afternoon trade.

Improved sentiment in equity markets bled into metals, too. Silver contracts jumped more than 9% to $43.68 a troy ounce, while gold futures added 3.6% to trade around $3,660 an ounce.

Oil prices continued to rise, with most-traded Brent crude contracts for February delivery nudging up 0.3% to trade close to $92 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contract added 1.7% to trade around $85.10 a barrel.

Treasurys weakened amid investors' shift back to risk and hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Ten-year yields rose more than 5.5 basis points to trade above 4.900%, while two-year yields rose toward 4.700%. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, with expectations for a quarter-point rise priced in at 99%, according to LSEG.

The dollar edged higher against a basket of global currencies but remained below highs hit earlier this week. Bitcoin was helped by broader ebullient market sentiment, rising 1.5% to trade around $61,670.

Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez looks to stay in power. Next week, Nvidia's reinstated Chief Executive Jensen Huang will appear in front of Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday.

data.title: Canada Nixes Call for Auto Sector Exemption From Carbon-Tax Framework — Market Talk
data.description:
0847 ET - Canada shoots down a call from the province of Ontario and Unifor, the union representing the country's autoworkers, to exempt motor-vehicle manufacturers from a federal industrial carbon tax. The demand by Ontario and Unifor is an effort to persuade Stellantis to rethink its plan to sell a Toronto-area factory. "Claims that industrial carbon pricing harms domestic auto manufacturing are misleading," says Canadian Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin. She adds federal greenhouse-gas emission standards for vehicles don't apply to Canadian-built vehicles destined for export, which Dabrusin says cover the vast majority of vehicles Stellantis produces in Canada. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)

0248 ET - Marlboro-maker Altria shouldn't have any problems funding a deal to buy London-listed peer Imperial Brands, Citi's Simon Hales and Sunny Wadhwani write. Applying a 30% premium the analysts estimate that Altria would need to find $40 billion in cash to buy the maker of Davidoff and Gauloises cigarettes. Altria could sell some or all of its $12 billion stake in AB InBev to help fund the deal, they say. AB InBev would likely want to buy some of those shares back if they were up for sale, the analysts add. Altria shares closed Wednesday at $76.28 and U.S. markets were closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. Imperial Brands closed 13% higher at 34.32 pounds on Thursday, marking its highest price since July 2017. (ian.walker@wsj.com)

0241 ET - A merger between Altria and Imperial Brands is likely to face U.S. antitrust concerns as the combined company would have over a 50% market share, Citi's Simon Hales and Sunny Wadhwani write. However, selling Imperial's U.S. combustible cigarette assets to a third party--such as Japan Tobacco--could resolve the issue. "There is considerable strategic logic for a deal from Altria's standpoint as it would diversify its footprint and provide it with much needed scale in NGPs," the analysts say. Citi has a neutral rating on Altria's stock and a $72.00 target price. Altria's shares closed Wednesday at $76.28 and U.S. markets were closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. data.title: US goods trade deficit widens sharply in October
data.description:
The US trade deficit in goods widened sharply in October as an AI infrastructure buildout continued to draw in imports at a rapid clip, potentially putting trade on course to again subtract from economic growth in the fourth quarter.

The goods trade shortfall increased 10.7%, or $14.4 billion to $149.5 billion last month, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the goods deficit at $133 billion.

Goods imports shot up $21.1 billion to $365.3 billion. Exports of goods increased $6.7 billion to $215.8 billion.

The government reported on Wednesday that trade sliced off 3.21 percentage points from gross domestic product growth in the third quarter. The drag was, however, more than offset by robust growth in consumer spending and business investment in equipment, mostly AI-related.

The economy grew at a 4.3% annualized rate last quarter after expanding at a 2.2% pace in the April-June period. Trade has not contributed to gross domestic product growth for four straight quarters, reflecting strong domestic demand.

data.title: French Economy Slips Into Recession as Exports Sag — WSJ
data.description:
By Matthew Dalton

PARIS — The French economy tipped into a recession in the third quarter as summer heat waves slowed Airbus's factories, complicating the government's plans to narrow its yawning budget deficit.

Gross domestic product fell 0.2% in the third quarter after declining slightly in the second quarter, French statistics agency Insee said Friday. Economists define a recession as two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth.

France faces a morass of economic problems: anemic consumer spending, weak investment, an economy highly reliant on public spending and an export sector that is acutely exposed to the fortunes of Airbus, the aeronautics giant based next to Toulouse.

Punishing heat waves in July pushed temperatures inside Airbus factories to over 104 degrees Fahrenheit, according to union officials. Airbus slowed production of its A330 and A321 models, French authorities said, dragging down France's overall exports by 1.6%.

The government is proposing nearly EUR50 billion, equivalent to $55 billion, in budget savings to lower its deficit to 5% of GDP next year. The deficit this year is forecast to hit 5.5% of GDP, the largest in the eurozone. That threatens to stunt growth even more for an economy in which public spending accounts for around 57% of GDP, among the highest in the developed world.

Data coming in since the end of the quarter showed that France's domestic spending was weaker than expected, said Pauline Meinzel, an economist at Insee.

"Foreign trade is declining and we have domestic demand growth that is zero in the third quarter," she said.

France typically enjoys a construction boom ahead of local elections as mayors seek to curry favor with voters through public works, Meinzel said. That dynamic helped boost local spending before the most recent votes in March of this year on a host of big-ticket projects, from a tram extension in Marseille that cost EUR320 million to a new sports complex south of Paris at EUR100 million. Local government spending in total jumped 3.4% in 2025.

"Now, we're in a period of transition; the teams have just been re-elected," she said. "We're really seeing a sharp decline in investment in public works."

The decline in public spending threatens to sow further discontent among French voters ahead of next year's presidential elections and is likely to help Marine Le Pen's antiestablishment candidacy.

data.title: The Week in Oil: Crude on Track for Weekly Gains As Middle East Attacks Worry Market
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Here is a look at what happened in oil markets during the week of Nov. 23-27 and what traders will be watching in the days ahead.

OVERVIEW: Oil prices are on track for weekly gains on Friday after three consecutive weekly losses as continuing attacks on Middle Eastern shipping and Saudi infrastructure raised regional supply concerns. Front-month Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, is down 0.3% to $96.35 a barrel, while WTI futures rise 1.5% to $84.95 a barrel.

MACRO: Major U.S. indexes are poised to finish higher after a volatile week marked by AI jitters. "Stock markets around the world are hoping to put the recent turmoil behind them, staging a decent rebound as the week and month draw to a close," said XM analyst Raffi Boyadjian. "The shortened trading week in the United States due to the Thanksgiving holiday has likely helped in restoring some calm to equity markets."

This week's economic data indicated persistent inflation, resilient growth, and a solid labor market. Focus now shifts to the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision next month, with traders already pricing in a 25-basis-point hike.

GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: With no meaningful progress in U.S.-Iran negotiations, regional tensions remain high. Continued attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman have kept maritime security and potential supply disruptions in focus.

Oil supplies have remained largely unaffected, according to Commerzbank analysts. However, that could change if Saudi Arabia is forced to reduce oil exports through Ras Tanura, especially as Houthi militants also threaten export terminals on the Red Sea.

Earlier this week, the Houthis claimed an attack on Ras Tanura, which is Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery. Meanwhile, a separate strike on the country's Jazan refinery sparked a fire and temporarily halted some operations, while a drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians.

SUPPLY AND DEMAND: Middle Eastern oil flows remain significantly below prewar levels, with Strait of Hormuz transits at just 31% of the preconflict baseline, according to preliminary data from Kpler.

Iraqi crude exports remain relatively strong despite delays to some November and December shipments, which Kpler attributed to oversold cargoes rather than falling production. Still, the delays have raised concerns over the reliability of prompt Middle Eastern supply, highlighting the market's sensitivity to short-term disruptions even in an otherwise well-supplied regional market, said Alex Booth, head of research at the data provider.

In the U.S., crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week as refineries increased capacity utilization, according to the latest Energy Information Administration data. Gasoline and distillate fuel stocks also climbed.

WHAT'S AHEAD: Attention now turns to Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, with some analysts expecting the group to hold current production quotas steady through January. With existing production agreements approaching their year-end deadline, key members of the group must decide how much oil each country can sustainably produce, and how much the cartel should collectively pump next year.

"It is quite possible that Sunday's OPEC+ meeting will end without a final decision and that current production quotas will initially remain in place, as OPEC delegates have indicated," said Commerzbank analyst Barbara Lambrecht. "With the exception of Iraq, production in most OPEC+ countries remains well below existing quotas, while some countries, including Russia, are unable to raise output any further."

Investors will also be watching for Saudi Arabia's official selling prices, which are set to be disclosed next week.

On the U.S. economic calendar, the ISM manufacturing and services PMI readings will provide further insight into the strength of the economy, while Jolts, ADP employment and weekly jobless claims will offer clues on labor market conditions ahead of Friday's November nonfarm payrolls report.
